title: How Volcanoes Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how volcanoes work, starting with a playful opening about the movie Joe Versus the Volcano. They cover Earth's layers (crust, mantle, inner core), the role of pressure in keeping mantle solid, plate tectonics, and how plate boundaries (spreading centers, subduction zones, transform boundaries) and hot spots produce volcanism. They explain magma versus lava, how magma rises, how dissolved gas and viscosity determine eruption style, and describe eruption types (Hawaiian, Strombolian, Plinian, Vulcanian, hydrovolcanic, fissure). They cover volcano shapes (stratovolcano, cinder cone, shield volcano), the parts of a volcano, Crater Lake as a caldera, and the active/dormant/extinct classification (about 500 active volcanoes). The episode closes with a New Year listener mail segment, including a listener's story about converting to Judaism and the Dradel variation in Israel.

segments.title: Opening banter and Joe Versus the Volcano
segments.summary: Hosts banter about the show's topic and the movie Joe Versus the Volcano, discussing the film's plot without spoiling it, and set up the episode on how volcanoes work.

segments.title: Earth's layers and pressure
segments.summary: Describes Earth's layers: the thin crust (about three miles thick under the ocean and up to about forty-four miles under land), the mantle, and the inner core. Explains that mantle rock is hot enough to melt but stays solid because of pressure.

segments.title: Plate tectonics and plate boundary volcanism
segments.summary: Covers continental drift and plate tectonics, with the plates moving over the asthenosphere. Explains spreading center volcanism, where plates pull apart and magma fills the gap, and subduction zone volcanism, where one plate slides under another and water lowers the melting point.

segments.title: Magma, lava, and transform boundaries
segments.summary: Defines magma as liquid rock underground and lava as magma once it exits the Earth. Describes collision zones and transform plate boundaries, where plates slide past each other and volcanic activity is almost never found.

segments.title: Hot spot volcanoes and the Hawaiian islands
segments.summary: Explains intraplate hot spot volcanism, where a mantle plume creates magma under a plate that forms a chain of volcanoes as the plate moves over it, using Hawaii as the example. Notes that most land volcanoes are subduction-related or hot spot, and most ocean volcanoes are spreading-center.

segments.title: Magma rising, gas, and viscosity
segments.summary: Explains how magma rises because it is less dense and seeks the path of least resistance, and how magma chambers form. Describes how dissolved gases form bubbles (vesicles) when vapor pressure rises, comparing this to a shaken soda can. Viscosity and gas content determine eruption style.

segments.title: Types of eruptions
segments.summary: Describes eruption types: effusive Hawaiian eruptions with slow lava flows, Strombolian bursts, Plinian eruptions like Vesuvius that send columns of material miles into the air, and the less common Vulcanian, hydrovolcanic, and fissure eruptions. Mentions the 2010 Iceland eruption and its airline disruption as likely Plinian.

segments.title: Sponsor reads and closing
segments.summary: Brief promotional content and closing remarks about volcanoes and website resources.
